clue.text: Feels soft clothes

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft
robes are garments, clothes

explanation.surface: Someone runs their fingers over soft garments.
explanation.definitionFit: To probe is to explore by touch, so it is a verb synonym for feels in the investigating sense.

clue.text: Run out on a National horse

parts.note: RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: A horse runs loose during the Grand National.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is Britain's most famous steeplechase, which the surface evokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A roan is a horse whose coat has white hairs mixed with a darker colour, an example of the animal.

clue.text: Help drivers to find remote places

parts.note: to back someone is to support or help them
woods are golf clubs used for driving the ball

explanation.surface: A satnav service helping motorists reach out-of-the-way spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drivers' suggests motorists, but they are golf clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: The backwoods are isolated, thinly settled forest regions far from towns.

clue.text: Show model short dress

parts.note: to sit for an artist is to model

indicators.note: short means cut, so the word for dress loses its last letter

parts.note: to comb hair is to dress it

explanation.surface: A fashion show where the model wears a short dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress' is a verb here, as in dressing hair: COMB, cut to COM.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitcom, short for situation comedy, is a type of television programme.

clue.text: For train, affected routes are detailed

indicators.note: affected here means altered or disturbed, so the letters are put in a new order
de-tailed: the word are loses its last letter, its tail

explanation.surface: A rail announcement: services have been diverted and the route changes are spelt out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' is not 'described in detail' but 'tail removed', turning ARE into AR; 'affected' then rearranges ROUTES plus AR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eurostar is the high-speed passenger service through the Channel Tunnel linking London with Paris and Brussels.

clue.text: Run through Kama Sutra's middle one: climax in new positions!

definitions.text: Run through Kama Sutra's middle one: climax in new positions!

indicators.note: new positions means the letters are set in a fresh arrangement
run through means pierced or killed, so a part of the name is removed

parts.note: the middle three letters of the nine in Kama Sutra are A, S, U

explanation.surface: A cheeky instruction to work through the Kama Sutra's central chapter and reach a climax in novel positions!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run through' removes ASU from KAMASUTRA, leaving KAMTRA; with ONE and CLIMAX, 'in new positions' rearranges the lot. The whole clue ends with the very symbol it describes.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation at the clue's end calls for the punctuation sign used after an excited cry, exactly what the clue's final symbol is.

clue.text: Dependent on tablet — necessary to get up

parts.note: re means on or concerning

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the letters read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: E is short for ecstasy, a tablet
vital means essential, necessary

explanation.surface: Someone reliant on a pill that they need just to get out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dependent on' reads as one phrase, but 'on' gives RE; 'get up' reverses E and VITAL to make LATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something relative depends on comparison with something else, so it is an adjective synonym for dependent.

clue.text: Exploit model in paper over time

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first part sits above the next
in puts the model's letter within the newspaper's name

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A tabloid exploits a model splashed across its pages for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exploit' is a noun, a daring feat; 'over' puts STUN above T.
explanation.definitionFit: A stunt is a daring feat done to impress, a synonym for exploit as a noun.

clue.text: Sorting bag later — is one dealing with problems involving letters?

definitions.text: one dealing with problems involving letters

indicators.note: sorting means arranging, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A postal worker sorting the mailbag later, handling problem letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' suggests post in the sorting office, but means the x and y of equations.
explanation.definitionFit: An algebraist is a mathematician working on equations where letters stand for unknown numbers.

clue.text: Went back to bed, one originally called number

indicators.note: back says the word for went is to be read in the opposite direction

parts.note: ran means went, as in went quickly
a cot is a small bed
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: originally points to the start of the next word, its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone retired to bed again after a phone call came in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' reads as a figure but is something that numbs; 'back' turns RAN into NAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic is a drug that dulls sensation, so it is literally a thing that makes you numb, a numb-er.

clue.text: Kill time in boxing ring with jab

indicators.note: in places the ring-shaped letter within the word for jab

parts.note: a lunge is a sudden thrust or jab
a ring is round, so it gives the letter O

explanation.surface: A boxer passes time in the ring throwing jabs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing ring' looks like a single sporting phrase, but it simply gives the circle-shaped O.
explanation.definitionFit: To lounge is to idle about lazily, which is a way of passing the hours, an idiom for killing time.

clue.text: Show Lewis Hamilton bio: not aware when taxed

indicators.note: taxed suggests strained or worked hard, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A racing driver's biography reveals he did not know he was being taxed.
explanation.walkthrough: All 24 letters of LEWIS HAMILTON BIO NOT AWARE rearrange into the quiz show's name; 'when' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a famous television quiz programme where contestants answer questions for a top prize of a million pounds.

clue.text: Me? Poser? Nude in centre spread all stripped

definitions.text: Me? Poser? Nude in centre spread all stripped

indicators.note: spread means scattered or laid out differently, so the letters are rearranged
in centre takes only the middle letters of nude
stripped means the word all loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: A glamour model protests her innocence while posing nude across a centrefold.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of NUDE gives UD and 'stripped' takes L from ALL; with ME and POSER, 'spread' rearranges them all.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue sketches a top fashion model posing for a centrefold, the kind of famous glamour figure the answer names.

clue.text: Tramp cut smell that might come out of armpit

definitions.text: that might come out of armpit

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the word for tramp loses its final letter

parts.note: a bum is a tramp or vagrant
BO is body odour, a smell

explanation.surface: A vagrant gives off an odour from under his arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' is also this setter's pseudonym, adding a joke at their own expense.
explanation.definitionFit: A bubo is an inflamed swollen lymph gland, typical of plague, that appears in the groin or armpit.

clue.text: 'Drink stock of vodka regularly', returning addicts admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the addicts' letters go inside
returning means the regularly picked letters are read backwards
regularly takes every other letter of the words stock of vodka

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, a group of addicts

explanation.surface: A slogan urging steady stocking of vodka, with recovering alcoholics in the picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes T, C, O, V, D, A from 'stock of vodka'; 'returning' gives ADVOCT, and 'admitted' puts AA inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Advocaat is a Dutch liqueur made with eggs, sugar and brandy, so it is an example of an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Chippy with fish written on board

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first part sits on top of the second

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
to board a ship or train is to enter it

explanation.surface: A fish-and-chip shop with fish chalked up on the menu board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chippy' suggests a fish-and-chip shop, the British takeaway, but is also slang for a woodworker.
explanation.definitionFit: Chippy is British slang for a woodworker who makes and fits timber fittings, from the wood chips produced.

clue.text: Topless senhorita excited unconventional leading man

indicators.note: excited means agitated, so the letters are stirred into a new order
topless means the word senhorita loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A topless Portuguese woman stirs up an unusual male lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' drops the S of SENHORITA; 'excited' rearranges ENHORITA.
explanation.definitionFit: An antihero is a protagonist lacking conventional heroic qualities, so a principal character who breaks the mould.

clue.text: City brothels in kinky houses

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the letters sit inside the words brothels in kinky

explanation.surface: A seedy tale of a city whose brothels are in kinky premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like a noun for buildings, but it is a verb meaning contains.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital of Finland, an example of a city.

clue.text: Got up to make drink

definitions.meaning: past tense of rise: stood or climbed out of bed
a pink wine, made with brief skin contact

explanation.surface: Someone rose to fix themselves a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose is the past tense of rise, meaning got up, and rosé is a pink wine.

clue.text: Call for attention, woman in lift well below this?

parts.note: oi is a shout to get someone's attention

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting means the letters read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: a girl is a young woman

explanation.surface: Someone shouts to a woman in an elevator going far below ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' looks like 'much', but is an oil well under the platform; 'in lift' reverses GIRL.
explanation.definitionFit: An offshore drilling platform sits above the oil well it taps, so the well lies beneath it.

clue.text: See 11
Look to leader from Brussels before campaign

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

indicators.note: leader from means the first letter of Brussels

parts.note: by can mean before, as in by noon

explanation.surface: Someone looks to an EU chief before launching a political campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'campaign' is a verb: to lobby is to campaign to influence lawmakers.
explanation.definitionFit: To lobby is to try to persuade politicians, a synonym for campaigning on an issue.

clue.text: Extra papers in the Guardian

indicators.note: in places the papers inside the newspaper's pronoun

parts.note: a newspaper refers to itself editorially as we
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: Extra pages appear in this newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a wide is a ball bowled out of reach, scoring an extra run; the Guardian speaking of itself is WE.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, extras are runs not scored off the bat, and a wide is one type of such run.

clue.text: OK to take in features of hotel room? Going off opening B&B?

indicators.note: going off means leaving, so each opening letter departs from the two items

parts.note: a bed and a Gideon Bible are standard items in a hotel room
the two letters B, the initials of the two room items

explanation.surface: A guest wonders whether it is safe to eat something in their room, or whether the guesthouse food has spoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'B&B' looks like bed and breakfast, but here it names the two first letters B: BED and BIBLE, each losing its B, give ED and IBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible food is fit to eat, acceptable to consume, so it is a synonym for safe to swallow.

clue.text: Runway show? Take clothes off

parts.note: to air something is to broadcast or show it
to strip is to undress

explanation.surface: A fashion show on the catwalk where the models undress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runway' suggests a catwalk, fitting 'show' and 'clothes', but here it is the landing strip for aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: An airstrip is a basic stretch of ground where planes take off and land, a synonym for runway.

clue.text: It's printed with parts from two magazines (first is short)

indicators.note: the first title loses its last letter, as a short word is cut off

parts.note: Playboy and OK! are two magazines

explanation.surface: A publication assembled from extracts of two magazines.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'parts' are roles for actors or plays in a sport, not pieces of magazines; PLAYBOY cut to PLAYBO, plus OK.
explanation.definitionFit: A playbook is a book of plays or a set of planned moves, printed out with the parts or roles set down.

clue.text: Turn over paper and study plot

indicators.note: turn over means the word for paper is flipped back to front

parts.note: a rag is a newspaper, usually a poor one
a den is a small private room, a study

explanation.surface: Someone flips their newspaper and studies a plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' tempts as the story, but it is a patch of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden is a plot of ground for growing plants, so plot is a synonym in its land sense.
